Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG evaluation we need compact evidence for the encryption & key management controls. Can you provide the following by end of week? Prefer single PDF bundle plus any CSV samples for logs.

1) HSM attestation describing model, tamper-resistance, FIPS level, and export controls (signed).
2) Key rotation chronology for customer-facing KMS keys (past 12 months) and a representative rotation log sample (CSV).
3) Proof that customer KMS keys are non-exportable / wrapped; explanation of any wrap/unwrap flows and KMIP/TLS controls in transit.
4) Access matrix for KMS operators (roles, MFA, break-glass procedure).
5) Retention policy for key material snapshots and cryptographic telemetry (how long rotation artifacts and HSM shift logs are kept).

If a 1-page summary addressing each item is easier, that works too — we mostly need artifacts we can attach to the SIG questionnaire.

Appreciate a quick reply on timing.

Best,

Thanks — added the rotation snapshot and retention wording. Key items:
- Rotation cadence: service-managed customer keys rotate on a 90-day schedule for ephemeral session keys; tenant root-wrapping keys are rotated on a 12-month cadence unless customer BYOK requests otherwise.
- Rotation artifact retention: rotation logs and key event records retained 2 years; HSM shiftlogs and tamper alerts retained 5 years.
- Attached is a redacted CSV sample of rotation events (timestamps, key_id hash, operator_id redacted).

Attachments (included):
- key-rotation-snapshot-2028-07.csv (text/csv, 28KB)

For the wrap/unwrap flow: we use envelope encryption. Customer data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated per-tenant, wrapped by tenant KEKs that live in the HSM. Unwrap operations require operator orchestration + KMS policy checks; plaintext KEKs are never persisted outside HSM memory.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Lead Cryptography Engineer, Redwood Inference
